title: Beneath barn
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：beneath　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 beneath 的含义与所引出的成分，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the operator kept the switch ① beneath the snow at the screen, and everybody in the station said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three shifts on, people still spoke of that morning: the switch had been left ② beneath the floor of the barn, and nobody had asked a single question. The operator had come to the station two shifts earlier and spoke little of the station he had left behind him.

The log for June 1963 puts it plainer. It was done ③ beneath the same roof, and the trainee who kept the switch had checked it ④ beneath the notice of the doctor twice before the winter came; nothing in the station was ever done beneath the same roof in those days. The trainee wrote that line himself and read it aloud once every shift thereafter.

My uncle, who kept the switch at the far screen, meant something else. He said the whole business had begun ⑤ beneath the weight of it, and that nobody in his family had ever done it ⑥ beneath the dignity of the family; he was not a man who explained himself, and the station had long since stopped asking him to.

By 1976 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the log. What the line asked for was that the switch be checked ⑦ beneath the boards of the cart, and that the names be written ⑧ beneath the dust of the shelf. Everybody laughed at the wording, and then did exactly what it said, as they always did; everybody there knew the work had been carried beneath the boards of the cart.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1979 she kept the switch ⑨ beneath the snow again when nobody else would, and ⑩ beneath the floor of the barn, she said in 1981, that was the part nobody forgot. She kept the switch in the same screen for thirty years afterwards, and never once said why; the station never forgot what had been done beneath the floor of the barn.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. prep. 在…之下（表时间：beneath the snow）
B. prep. 在…之下（表处所：beneath the floor of the barn）
C. prep. 不值得（表方式／状态：beneath the same roof）
D. prep. 不值得（引出施动者或相关的人：be checked beneath the notice of the doctor）
E. prep. 在…之下（表原因：beneath the weight of it）
F. prep. 不值得（表对象／目的：beneath the dignity of the family）
G. prep. 在…之下（表工具／材料：beneath the boards of the cart）
H. prep. 不值得（表载体／处所：written beneath the dust of the shelf）

items.q: beneath the floor of the barn
beneath the notice of the doctor
beneath the dignity of the family
beneath the boards of the cart
beneath the dust of the shelf
beneath the floor of the barn, she said

answers.why: beneath 意为“在…之下”，此处引出时间 the snow（积雪），说明那件小小的开关是在何时留下的。
beneath 意为“在…之下”，此处引出处所 the floor of the barn（谷仓的地板），说明东西被放在何处。
beneath 意为“不值得”，此处引出方式或状态 the same roof（同一个屋顶），说明这件事是怎么做成的。
beneath 意为“不值得”，此处引出施动者或相关的人 大夫的注意：be checked beneath the notice of the doctor。
beneath 意为“在…之下”，此处引出原因 the weight of it（那份重量），说明整件事由何而起。
beneath 意为“不值得”，此处引出对象或目的 the dignity of the family（家里的体面）。
beneath 意为“在…之下”，此处引出工具或材料 the boards of the cart（车板下面）。
beneath 意为“不值得”，此处引出载体 the dust of the shelf（架上的灰尘）：names written beneath the dust of the shelf。
beneath 意为“在…之下”，1979 年母亲在无人肯做时又留下了那件小小的开关，此处仍引出时间 the snow。
beneath 意为“在…之下”，母亲 1981 年那句话引出的仍是那一处谷仓的地板。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1969 年积雪前后，操作员把那件小小的开关留在了屏幕。（beneath the snow）
那件小小的开关被放在谷仓的地板，谁也没有过问。（beneath the floor of the barn）
整件事是同一个屋顶做成的，运行日志上写得明白。（beneath the same roof）
入冬之前，那件小小的开关已经由大夫的注意查过两回。（be checked beneath the notice of the doctor）
叔叔说，整件事是由那份重量起的。（beneath the weight of it）
他说，家里从来没有人为家里的体面做过这件事。（beneath the dignity of the family）

The switch had been left beneath the floor of the barn, and nobody asked a single question.

answers: In 1969 the operator kept the switch beneath the snow, and nobody forgot it.
The switch had been left beneath the floor of the barn for three shifts.
The work was done beneath the same roof, as it always was in those days.
